summary: stro-Nova is a lunar landing-site analysis platform designed to help explore and evaluate potential landing locations near the Moon’s South Pole. It combines NASA planetary datasets and scientific calculations to provide insights into lunar terrain and the surrounding space environment.
details:
Astro-Nova – Lunar Landing Site Navigator

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

Astro-Nova is an interactive lunar landing-site analysis platform focused on exploring potential landing locations near the Moon's South Pole. It brings together planetary terrain data and astronomical calculations to help users understand the characteristics and environmental conditions of selected lunar sites.

The platform uses high-resolution Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) datasets to examine elevation, surface slope, terrain characteristics, and surrounding horizon obstructions. It analyzes 360-degree horizon profiles to identify the highest observed terrain obstruction along different directions.

The project also integrates NASA/JPL Horizons ephemeris data to calculate the apparent positions of the Sun and Earth for a selected location and observation time. Users can explore candidate locations, visualize available analysis results, and compare terrain information through an interactive dashboard.

2. What are its benefits?

  • Combines multiple lunar scientific datasets and calculations in one platform.
  • Makes complex planetary terrain information easier to explore and understand.
  • Provides elevation, slope, and horizon obstruction information for selected locations.
  • Helps examine Sun and Earth positions at specific observation times.
  • Supports preliminary comparison of potential lunar landing environments.
  • Clearly communicates data coverage, uncertainties, and scientific limitations.

3. What is the intended impact?

Future lunar exploration, particularly near the lunar South Pole, requires a detailed understanding of surface conditions and the surrounding space environment. Astro-Nova aims to make relevant scientific information more accessible to students, researchers, and space exploration enthusiasts.

The long-term vision is to support preliminary lunar site assessment by bringing terrain intelligence and astronomical visibility information together. It is designed as an exploratory decision-support platform, not as a certified landing-safety system.

4. What technologies and tools were used?

Programming languages:

  • JavaScript
  • Python
  • HTML
  • CSS

Frontend and software:

  • React.js
  • Vite
  • Node.js
  • Express-style HTTP backend
  • Three.js / React Three Fiber for 3D visualization
  • Git and GitHub
  • Visual Studio Code

Scientific datasets and services:

  • NASA Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) data
  • NASA/JPL Horizons System
  • Lunar South Pole high-resolution topography datasets

Scientific processing:

  • Raster-based elevation and slope analysis
  • Terrain horizon calculations
  • Lunar polar stereographic coordinate transformations
  • Astronomical ephemeris data parsing and validation

5. How is the project creative and innovative?

Astro-Nova combines lunar terrain analysis and astronomical observations in a single interactive environment. Instead of presenting isolated scientific datasets, it connects terrain characteristics with the apparent positions of the Sun and Earth from selected candidate locations.

Its 360-degree horizon analysis examines terrain obstruction in multiple directions, while its interactive dashboard makes the results easier to interpret. The combination of scientific computation, 3D lunar visualization, and candidate-site exploration creates an accessible way to investigate complex lunar environments.

6. What factors did the team consider?

Our team considered:

  • Scientific reliability: Using authentic NASA datasets and JPL services wherever applicable.
  • Terrain characteristics: Examining elevation, slope, surface variation, and horizon obstructions.
  • Observation conditions: Considering Sun and Earth positions at specified UTC observation times.
  • Data limitations: Accounting for incomplete raster coverage, measurement uncertainty, and interpolation limitations.
  • Coordinate accuracy: Respecting lunar coordinate systems and map projections.
  • Usability: Creating an understandable and interactive interface for exploring scientific results.
  • Future scalability: Designing the platform so that additional lunar datasets and analysis modules can be integrated.

Astro-Nova is an independent student-developed project inspired by the goal of making lunar exploration data more understandable and useful for preliminary scientific investigation.
